newsitem.title: USA: Calif. officials critical of pension fund returns.
newsitem.headline: Calif. officials critical of pension fund returns.

text.p: California's $68 billion State Teachers' Retirement System (STRS) drew fire on Monday from top state officials who were critical of the pension fund's recent investment performance.

The STRS fund was outperformed by the California Public Employees' Retirement System (CalPERS) by over 300 basis points last year, according to figures distributed by state Controller Kathleen Connell. The 300 basis points represented $1.8 billion of earnings.
"The controller is deeply dismayed by the performance of STRS," a spokesman for Connell said Monday.
California state Treasurer Matt Fong has also expressed concerns about the fund's recent performance but warned against overreacting to the short-term numbers.
"Like many trustees, Treasurer Fong has concerns about the short-term trend," Fong spokesman Stan Devereux said Monday.
Last week, Fong's representative on the STRS board introduced a motion directing the retirement system's chief investment officer to report back to the board in March on the status of the portfolio.
As of December 31, 1996, the market value of the California State Teachers' Retirement System investment portfolio was $67.9 billion.
STRS had a 9.9 percent investment gain for the year ending December 31, versus the 12.9 percent of CalPERS.
CalPERS is the largest public pension system in the U.S. with more than $100 billion in assets.
